title: The average of three attempts
one: Three numbers in, one average out, kept in Global.cs.

stages.title: Check what your average button has

screens.title: Check what your average button already does
screens.goal: I check the average button has code, refuses letters, and shows 6 for 5, 6 and 7.

blocks.p: Your average button may have some code already. This screen checks what is there.

check.what: In the Design tab, double-click the average button. Is there code between its curly brackets?
check.how: The code tab opens at btnCalculateAverage_Click. Lines between the curly brackets mean yes.

check.what: Run it. Type letters in an attempt box and press the button. Does a number only message appear?
check.how: Use the green Start arrow. Log in and fill in the details first.

check.what: Type 5, 6 and 7 and press the button. Does 6 appear and the quiz panel switch on?
check.how: The average shows in the box beside the button.

screens.title: Start the average button by saying every box is right
screens.goal: The average button starts with a bool called passValidation set to true. Any failed check turns it false.

blocks.p: The average button checks the three attempt boxes before it adds them up.
It starts by saying every box is right. Any check that fails changes that to wrong.

words: Not. It turns true into false.
Is every character a number from 0 to 9?
Turn the words in a box into a number with a point.
Cut a number down to 2 numbers after the point.
Turn a number back into words, so a box can show it.
blocks.intro: Five new things in this chapter. Click any marked word to see what it means.

steps.do: In the Design tab, double-click the average button.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnCalculateAverage_Click.

code.title: The average button, part 1 of 8
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnCalculateAverage_Click
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
Trust the boxes
passValidation means did every box pass? It is a bool, true or false. It starts true.

blocks.watch: passValidation starts true. Only a failed check turns it false.

screens.title: Turn passValidation false when a box is empty
screens.goal: If any of the three attempt boxes is empty, passValidation is set to false.

blocks.p: The first check asks: is any of the three boxes empty?
It is the same question as on the Enter button, asked three times. Two straight lines mean or.

code.title: The average button, part 2 of 8
partLines: Is a box empty?
Is attempt 1 empty, OR attempt 2, OR attempt 3? It is all one line.
Then do not trust them
passValidation becomes false.

blocks.watch: Type the question as one long line. Visual Studio wraps it for you.

screens.title: Turn passValidation false when attempt 1 holds a letter
screens.goal: If the first attempt box holds something that is not a number from 0 to 9, passValidation is set to false.

blocks.p: The next check asks: does a box hold anything that is not a number?
[[.All(char.IsDigit)|1]] asks if every character is a number. [[!|0]] in front turns the answer round.
So the question means: is it NOT all numbers?

code.title: The average button, part 3 of 8
partLines: Attempt 1 not all numbers?
Is the first box NOT all numbers?
Then do not trust them
passValidation becomes false.

blocks.watch: The ! goes straight in front of the box name. There is no space.

screens.title: Do the same check for attempts 2 and 3
screens.goal: The same letter check is done for the second and third attempt boxes.

blocks.p: Now the same check for the other two boxes. Only the box name changes.

code.title: The average button, part 4 of 8
partLines: Attempt 2 not all numbers?
The same check for the second box.
Attempt 3 not all numbers?
The same check for the third box.

blocks.watch: Each check names a different box. Check you changed the 1 to 2, then to 3.

screens.title: Show a message and empty the boxes if a check failed
screens.goal: If passValidation is false, a message asks for numbers only and the three boxes are emptied.

blocks.p: Now every check is done. If passValidation is false, something was wrong.

code.title: The average button, part 5 of 8
partLines: Did a check fail?
Is passValidation false?
Say so and empty the boxes
A message box asks for numbers only. The three boxes are emptied.

blocks.watch: Two equals signs ask a question. One equals sign would change passValidation.

screens.title: Add the three attempts, divide by 3 and round
screens.goal: The three attempts are added, divided by 3, rounded to 2 places, kept in Global.cs and shown in the box.

blocks.p: else runs when every box held a number. Now the average is worked out.
A box holds words. [[Convert.ToDouble|2]] turns them into a number that can have a point.
[[Math.Round(x, 2)|3]] keeps 2 numbers after the point. [[.ToString()|4]] turns the number back into words for the box.

code.title: The average button, part 6 of 8
partLines: Add and divide
else, then the three attempts are added and divided by 3. It is all one line.
Round it
roundedAv keeps 2 numbers after the point.
Keep it and show it
The average goes into Global.cs, the file you made in chapter 3. Then the box beside the button shows it.

blocks.watch: The brackets round the three numbers matter. Without them only the last one is divided by 3.

screens.title: Save the three attempts in Global.cs and switch off the attempts panel
screens.goal: Global.cs notes the average is worked out and keeps the three attempts. The attempts panel switches off.

blocks.p: Next, the average button notes the average is done. It saves the three attempts in Global.cs too.
Convert.ToInt32 turns the words in a box into a whole number.

code.title: The average button, part 7 of 8
partLines: Worked out. Switch off this panel
averageCalculated becomes true. The attempts panel switches off.
Keep the three attempts
Each attempt goes into its line in Global.cs as a whole number.

blocks.watch: else opens with a curly bracket. Its closing curly bracket comes in part 8.

screens.title: Switch on the quiz panel
screens.goal: After the attempts are kept, the quiz panel switches on so the pupil can move on.

blocks.p: Last, the average button moves the pupil on to the quiz.

flow.before: The average is worked out. The button is pressed.
flow.say: The attempts panel goes grey and switches off. The quiz panel switches on.
